summary: Ross County, Ohio tower planned on Farrell Hill: land given 1935, construction reported started by September 1937 as a 73-foot field tower; index lists it gone, no removal date found.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts index lists the site as 'Tower Gone'; no source dates its removal or says what remains

events.note: Acre on Farrell Hill given by P.T.C. Brown, Jr. for a fire lookout tower; announced in the Chillicothe Gazette, 6 December 1935

Construction reported started by 9 September 1937 (planned 73-foot field tower; CCC crews from Camp Pike to extend the access road). Completion date not found; the January 1936 notice had expected erection early in 1936

evidence.supports: acre donated on Farrell Hill by P.T.C. Brown, Jr., for use as a fire lookout tower (Dec 1935 item)
evidence.quote: Donation of an acre of ground on Farrell Hill by P.T.C. Brown , Jr., real estate dealer of 54 East Second street, for use as a fire lookout tower

evidence.supports: January 1936 notice expected erection early in 1936
evidence.quote: It is anticipated that the tower will be erected early in the present year.

evidence.supports: construction of the tower at California Hollow, between Bourneville and Bainbridge, had started by September 1937
evidence.quote: Construction of a new forest fire tower on Farrell Hill at California Hollow, between Bourneville and Bainbridge, has been started
It will be a 73-foot field tower

evidence.supports: CCC boys of Camp Pike to extend the California Hollow road a mile to the tower
evidence.quote: CCC boys of Camp Pike will extend the California Hollow road a mile to the tower to make it accessible by automobile.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts files the tower under Ohio Dept of Natural Resources
Ohio index marks Farrell Hill (Ross County) as Tower Gone, FFLOS US 1557, OH 3
evidence.quote: Farrell Hill Ross 39.26250 -83.23380 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1557, OH 3

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page places the tower in Ross County
announced by an Associate State Forester (the 'state forestry official' in the story)
evidence.quote: was announced today by Associate State Forester B. E. Leete

evidence.supports: proposed tower site at the top of the hill
evidence.quote: at the top of the hill

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 22.3 matches the 73-foot height announced in the 1937 item; it is a plan, not a measured height. Brief record otherwise matches sources; no corrections. Built completion and removal dates are not in any source read. Unverified lead, not used in the story: waymarking.com page 'Bainbridge Gap Filler, Bainbridge, Ohio' (https://www.waymarking.com/waymarks/wm5G6V_Bainbridge_Gap_Filler_Bainbridge_Ohio) appears to say a Farrell Hill Fire Tower stood nearby, erected in 1938 and dismantled in August 1978. fetch_text returned only the page title and the wording came from a WebFetch summary, so it does not pass the quote check; verify on the live page before use. If confirmed, the 1938 erection date would conflict with the 1937 construction report.
